clue.text: Cutting attack on ultimately debatable description by one nation's leader, it was said

parts.note: a stab is an attack with a blade, a cutting attack

indicators.note: ultimately points to the closing letters of the word debatable, here its last two

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, a description of the facts
the Roman numeral for one is I
the US is the nation, the United States

explanation.surface: A sharp critique of a disputed phrase a national leader once used about himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the last two letters of 'debatable'; 'on' and 'by' only join the pieces. The definition plays on the boast a US president made about himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump called himself a very stable genius, so the phrase names a leader by his own claim.

clue.text: Stroppy sailor, one in country upset you previously, right?

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the reversed country
upset in a down clue means the country is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Wales is a country of the UK
one gives A, the indefinite article
ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A sailor asks whether someone had once been upset in a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns WALES into SELAW, with A 'in' it: SEALAW, then YE and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea lawyer is a sailor who argues about orders and rights, a troublesome crew member.

clue.text: One restaurant has a no-show — wait here

parts.note: an means one, the indefinite article

indicators.note: no-show means the letter named before it fails to appear in the restaurant word

parts.note: a tearoom is a small restaurant serving tea
the letter a, as written in the clue

explanation.surface: A diner is left waiting when a booking fails to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'no-show' is a diner who misses a booking; here it is the deletion signal, and 'wait here' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An anteroom is a small outer room where visitors wait before entering.

clue.text: Clear Spanish leader's pointlessly arrested unionist

indicators.note: arrested means held, so one piece is caught inside another
pointlessly removes a compass point, here the letter E for east

parts.note: El Cid was the medieval Castilian military leader
U is the abbreviation for Unionist in politics

explanation.surface: A Spanish leader has a unionist locked up for no reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointlessly' drops E (a compass point) from EL CID, and LCID has U 'arrested' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid means clear, as in easy to understand.

clue.text: Good doctor detained by those in charge — they're not happy

indicators.note: detained by means held inside, so the doctor sits within the rulers

parts.note: rulers are those in charge
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Authorities hold a decent doctor, and people are unhappy about it.
explanation.walkthrough: G, then RULERS with MB 'detained by' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumblers are complainers, people discontented enough to moan.

clue.text: Want to give a false impression — not content to provoke

parts.note: to want is to need

indicators.note: not content means the inside of the word goes, leaving only its outside

parts.note: to lie is to give a false impression

explanation.surface: Someone longs to mislead, being dissatisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not content' empties the word of its middle, here a single letter; 'content' is what is contained, not 'satisfied'.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to irritate or goad them.

clue.text: Where young people go to learn about having sex

parts.words: Where young people go to learn
parts.note: uni is short for university, where students study
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A coy description of sex education at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' only links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Union in the sense of physical coupling is a polite word for sexual intercourse.

clue.text: Tolerated politicians coming through window

indicators.note: coming through means the politicians pass into the middle of the other word

parts.note: let means allowed, tolerated
the ANC is South Africa's African National Congress party

explanation.surface: Permitted MPs climb in through a window.
explanation.walkthrough: ANC 'coming through' LET: L-ANC-ET.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancet is a tall narrow pointed-arch window in Gothic architecture.

clue.text: Parting remark mentioned copper's make-up

indicators.note: mentioned means said out loud, so the letters are heard as spoken words

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, its elemental make-up

explanation.surface: A police officer's farewell, said as they put on cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' is the metal, not a police officer; CU spoken as letters says the farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: See you is a casual goodbye said when people part.

clue.text: Change at home going back inside

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece sits within the word at
going back means the word for home is read from right to left

parts.note: a pad is informal for a home or flat

explanation.surface: Someone moving house has to adjust to a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' reverses the word for home before it goes 'inside'; 'Change' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt is to alter or modify, a verb of change.

clue.text: Stop bleeding — gold tunic's front covered in red

indicators.note: covered in places the gold and tunic pieces wrapped inside the red colour

parts.note: cerise is a cherry-red colour
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: front picks out the opening letter of tunic

explanation.surface: First aid: a wounded soldier's golden tunic is soaked in blood.
explanation.walkthrough: AU plus T (the front of 'tunic's') is 'covered in' CERISE: CER-AUT-ISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cauterising seals a wound by burning, which halts the flow of blood.

clue.text: Burnt vegetable while chatting

indicators.note: while chatting means the word is heard in speech rather than seen written

parts.note: chard is a leafy green vegetable

explanation.surface: A cook overdoes the greens while gossiping.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARD said in conversation sounds like CHARRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Charred food has been scorched black, burnt on the surface.

clue.text: Lacking friends in past? Nonsense!

indicators.note: in places the friendless word inside the word for past

parts.note: by means past, as in walking by
someone with no friends is alone

explanation.surface: Someone protests at the claim they had no friends in their youth.
explanation.walkthrough: ALONE goes 'in' BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Baloney is slang for rubbish talk, a dismissive exclamation like 'rubbish!'.

clue.text: Destroy oil supply? He's not really a warrior

indicators.note: supply is read as supple-ly, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A saboteur blows up the fuel lines of an enemy army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' as an adverb (in a supple way) is the anagram signal for DESTROY OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's plaything figure in uniform is a soldier only in miniature, not a real fighter.

clue.text: Band initially attracted by modest reduction

indicators.note: attracted by means pulled into, so the band goes inside the modest word

parts.note: decent means modest, proper
R.E.M. is a rock band whose name is written as initials

explanation.surface: A group is drawn to a small cut in price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' tells us the band's name is written as initials, R.E.M.; 'attracted by' places it inside the modest word.
explanation.definitionFit: A decrement is a decrease, an amount by which something is lowered.

clue.text: Finished attempt to review secret police

indicators.note: to review is read as re-view, look back, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: up means finished, as in time is up
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone finishes a test and goes back over their answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to review' read as re-view, look again backwards, turns the whole charade round. The OGPU preceded the NKVD and KGB.
explanation.definitionFit: The OGPU was the Soviet state security service of the 1920s and 1930s, a political police force.

clue.text: Money in America made by Evian?

parts.note: the brand name Evian is naive written backwards; green means naive, and back says turn it round

explanation.surface: Asks whether dollars are made by a bottled water company.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as instructions, GREEN (naive) BACK (written backwards), and you get EVIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenback is a nickname for the US dollar bill, printed in green ink.

clue.text: Witty exchange not standing the test of time?

definitions.text: not standing the test of time?
definitions.meaning: read as ..., something that gets worse as it gets older

explanation.surface: Clever repartee that dates quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is light teasing banter; split as bad in age it describes something that ages poorly.

clue.text: Rent out finally with deposit

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word out

parts.note: ore is a mineral deposit in rock

explanation.surface: A tenant pays the rent at last, with a deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: T, the last letter of 'out', then ORE. 'Rent' is the past tense of rend, not payment for a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent and tore are both past tenses meaning ripped apart.

clue.text: Attempt to stop designer breaking story

indicators.note: breaking means the designer splits the story word open

parts.note: a tale is a story
CK stands for Calvin Klein, the fashion designer

explanation.surface: A designer interrupts a narrative trying to block it.
explanation.walkthrough: CK 'breaking' TALE: TA-CK-LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle an opponent in football or rugby is to try to halt them.

clue.text: Sports people in training resist cake

indicators.note: in training suggests the letters are being worked into shape, a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Athletes preparing for competition must turn down dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in training' rearranges RESIST CAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice skaters are athletes of a winter sport, so they are sporting people.

clue.text: Fume — female's taken part of course over

indicators.note: taken means held, so one piece is taken inside the female word

parts.note: she is a female, and the apostrophe s reads as has

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the golf word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a tee is part of a golf course, where each hole starts

explanation.surface: A woman playing golf is furious after losing ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'female's taken' reads as 'female has taken'; 'over' turns the golf piece upside down in this down clue before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to be inwardly furious, to rage.

clue.text: Walk round China — short run included

indicators.note: included means placed inside, so the run sits within the friend

parts.note: china is rhyming slang, china plate for mate, so pal

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a trot is a slow run

explanation.surface: Someone's walk around China includes a brief jog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate. TROT 'short' is TRO, 'included' in PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To patrol is to walk round an area to keep guard.

clue.text: See fragile ice melt in case study subject

parts.note: the letter C is pronounced see

indicators.note: fragile suggests something that breaks apart, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Look at how delicate ice thaws in an example being studied.
explanation.walkthrough: C, the letter that sounds like 'See', then 'fragile' rearranges ICE MELT IN CASE. 'case study' looks like one phrase, but 'case' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of climate is an academic discipline, a subject one can study.

clue.text: At first, silent sneeze a problem

indicators.note: at first, silent says the opening letters of the sneeze go unvoiced, leaving only its spoken sound

parts.note: atishoo is the British spelling of a sneeze; with its opening a and t not voiced, ishoo is left

explanation.surface: At first there is a quiet sneeze, then trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: ATISHOO is the British way of writing a sneeze. 'At first, silent' mutes its opening AT, and the rest is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a matter of concern, a difficulty to deal with.

clue.text: See 22
Hit largely overwhelming Posh Spice

indicators.note: overwhelming means surrounding, so the hit word swallows up the posh letter
largely means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: to smack is to hit
U means upper-class, the posh register in British usage

explanation.surface: A hit song mostly drowns out the famous Spice Girl Posh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posh Spice' was Victoria Beckham's Spice Girls name; here 'Posh' is U (upper-class) and 'Spice' the definition. SMACK 'largely' is SMAC, 'overwhelming' U.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a tangy reddish spice made from dried berries.

clue.text: Extremely articulate! Rambles? Wrong — one maintains a sharp focus

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are set out incorrectly, in a different order
extremely takes the first and last letters of articulate

explanation.surface: Someone praises eloquence, then wonders if it is rambling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives A and E (the first and last letters of 'articulate'); 'Wrong' rearranges them with RAMBLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser produces a tightly concentrated beam of light, held to a narrow point.

clue.text: A crack brings shame

parts.note: a crack is a try, and so is a bash, as in have a bash

explanation.surface: Trying something and failing is embarrassing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' means an attempt, not a split.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash is to make someone embarrassed, to humiliate them.

clue.text: At last, some clarity — flipping hell, it's a wake-up call

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the letters are tossed into a new order
at last takes the closing letter of the word some

parts.note: heck is the mild stand-in people say for hell

explanation.surface: Someone exasperated finally understands the situation and swears.
explanation.walkthrough: E (the last of 'some') with CLARITY, rearranged by 'flipping', gives REALITYC; then HECK. 'flipping hell' reads as an oath, but 'flipping' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A reality check is a jolt that brings someone back to the facts, an alerting reminder.
